notes: An address you type into a client no longer jumps back. Only static clients get a dnsmasq dhcp-host reservation, so an address typed into a dynamic row never reached the device -- it kept its pool address while the UI showed one nothing used -- and the lease importer then saw the row disagree with the lease and synced it back. Confirmed on a live router: a client stuck at 20.20.255.209 with ip_type dynamic and no dhcp-host line, while two sibling ports at 20.20.2.1 and 20.20.2.2 stayed put because they were static. An address an admin types is a reservation, so an explicit IP change now makes the row static, the same way attaching a proxy or opening a NAT port already does. Two more faults found while investigating a Wi-Fi RustDesk session that kept stalling, both the router's own doing: the ARP sweep pinged the whole DHCP range every 30 seconds, and roughly 240 of its 254 addresses are empty, so each pass was a burst of broadcast ARP -- measured at 199 packets/s out versus 71 in, with 253 of 268 neighbour entries INCOMPLETE/FAILED. It now runs every 10 minutes and skips addresses already belonging to a known client; DHCP devices are still found within 5 seconds without any broadcast. And a PPPoE port with no cable was dialled forever (carrier=0, service active, 180 discovery failures an hour); the unit now waits for the port to carry link before dialling. Release gate: 45 tests, up from 34.
